newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro shares maintain rally ahead of US open.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro shares maintain rally ahead of US open.

text.p: Europe's leading stock markets marched higher on Wednesday, buoyed by Wall Street's huge overnight gain and a sprinkling of good corporate results.
London, Frankfurt and Paris all stood well ahead by midday, with the German bourse's 1.60 percent gain leading the way in the wake of New York's rally on Tuesday.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed 2.60 percent higher -- its second largest one-day gain -- as investors charged into blue-chip stocks.
Paris and London also both rose over one percent during the morning, with the latter shrugging off an opinion poll pointing towards a hung parliament in Britain's May 1 general election.
Neither took much note of a thoroughly well-leaked report from the European Commission, which forecast all but Italy and Greece achieving a crucial target to join a single European currency.

The news stirred the lira in an otherwise quiet currency market. It sagged against the mark, although nerves were later soothed by a footnote in the report indicating the country could still meet a 1997 budget deficit-to-GDP target of 3.0 percent.
The dollar paid scant attention to the report and held steady, trading a shade under session highs against the mark and yen.
Amsterdam and Stockholm bourses also pushed higher, with good results from Volvo and Philips aiding a generally firm tone.
Shares in the Dutch electronics giant raced to an all-time high of 100.70 guilders after it posted a 22 percent surge in ordinary net profits as its consumer products arm swung back into the black.
The rise helped lift Amsterdam's AEX Index nearly two percent to 763 points.
Volvo shares jumped 6.5 crowns to 200 after the car maker reported a 60 percent rise in first quarter operating income, bolstering the Stockholm index, which stood up over one percent by midday.
Trade in London was spiced by an opinion poll suggesting a much reduced lead for the opposition Labour Party ahead of next week's May 1 election.
"We had a predictable mark-up on the back of Wall Street but there is still a lot of uncertainty out there," said a senior dealer.
"The latest opinion poll, if true, suggests there could be a hung parliament. That is something the market does not want to see," he said.

The ICM poll in The Guardian newspaper slashed Labour's lead from 14 to five points, the first time it has slipped to single figures since November 1993. But Gallup's survey in the Daily Telegraph put the gap up five points to 21.
French shares rallied just over one percent at the opening, reviving from a depression caused by political uncertainty ahead of this week's news of French parliamentary elections from late May.
Traders said Wall Street's rise and firmer bonds helped, as well as a more relaxed reading of the French political situation.

"The political risk is not so tremendous," one Paris broker said. The French government is seeking to confirm its position in power ahead of taking tough measures to ensure qualification for European economic and monetary union.
Further progress in Europe's key markets will hinge on how Wall Street opens, following the Dow Jones' 173.38 point gain to 6,833.59 on Tuesday.
In points terms, this was the second largest gain after an 187-point leap two days after the "Black Monday" stock market crash of October 1987, when the Dow lost 508 points.
"We'll stay around these levels until we get more of a clue what Wall Street's going to do this afternoon," said another London dealer.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7145 marks and 126.10 yen after ending at 1.7131 and 126.21 in late trading in Europe on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 49.3 points or 1.13 percent at 4,395.2.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was 55.62 points or 1.67 percent higher at 3,395.95.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 30.13 points or 1.20 percent at 2,544.80.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $340.70 an ounce, compared with Tuesday's London close of $341.65. Silver slipped three cents to $4.73.
